objective: Explain MFA, password policies and sessions
stem: Which authentication method is required for all user-interface logins to Salesforce?

options.text: Security questions that users answer when they log in
An SMS code only, which is sent to the user's phone
An email link only, which is sent to the user's inbox

explanation: Salesforce requires MFA for every user logging in to the UI. SSO users meet this through their identity provider.

objective: Explain MFA, password policies and sessions
stem: A user logs in using single sign-on through the company identity provider. How is the MFA requirement met?
explanation: With SSO, the identity provider handles authentication, including MFA.

objective: Tell login IP ranges from trusted IP ranges
stem: The CEO wants finance users to be able to log in only from the head office network. What should the admin configure?

options.text: Login IP ranges on the Finance profile
Trusted IP ranges set on the whole org
Field history tracking on the Finance profile
A sharing rule that limits records to the head office

explanation: Login IP ranges on a profile block logins from other addresses. Trusted IP ranges do not block anyone.

objective: Tell login IP ranges from trusted IP ranges
stem: What does adding a trusted IP range in Network Access do?

options.text: Users logging in from that range are not asked for identity verification
It blocks every login that comes from other IP addresses
It grants admin rights to users in that range
It encrypts the connection for users in that range

explanation: Trusted IP ranges skip the identity verification prompt but do not block access from elsewhere.

objective: Tell login IP ranges from trusted IP ranges
stem: Which setting limits the times of day a profile can log in?
explanation: Login hours are configured on the profile. Business hours are for support, not security.

objective: Explain MFA, password policies and sessions
stem: Which setting decides how long an inactive user stays logged in?
explanation: Session settings include the idle timeout, which logs users out after a period of inactivity.

objective: Explain MFA, password policies and sessions
stem: Which password policy setting locks an account after repeated wrong attempts?

options.text: Password history, which stops users reusing old passwords
Minimum length, which sets the shortest allowed password
Complexity requirement, which sets the mix of characters

explanation: The invalid login attempts setting locks the account. An admin can then unlock it.

objective: Describe single sign-on and connected apps
stem: What is single sign-on (SSO)?

options.text: Logging in with a company identity instead of a separate Salesforce password
Using a single profile for all users so that nobody needs separate permissions
Using one password for every Salesforce org that a company owns
A type of sharing rule that gives one user access to every record

explanation: SSO lets an identity provider prove who the user is, and Salesforce trusts it.

objective: Describe single sign-on and connected apps
stem: What is a connected app?

options.text: The way an external application is allowed to connect to Salesforce
A custom object that stores integration credentials
A permission set that gives an app access to all objects
A page layout used for the mobile app

explanation: Connected apps let external apps, such as mobile apps and integrations, authenticate with Salesforce, and admins control who may use them.

stem: How many fields per object can be tracked with standard field history tracking?
explanation: Standard field history tracking can track up to 20 fields per object.

stem: Which tool shows which setup changes were made and by whom?
explanation: Setup Audit Trail records configuration changes for 180 days.

stem: Which tool shows who logged in, from where, and whether the login succeeded?
explanation: Login History lists login attempts with IP address and status.

stem: The business wants to see old and new values for the Credit Limit field on accounts. What should the admin use?
explanation: Field history tracking stores old and new values of selected fields on records.

stem: Which tool provides detailed activity data, such as who exported a report?
explanation: Event Monitoring is a paid add-on that logs detailed user activity.

stem: The company needs encryption at rest for sensitive standard and custom fields and files. Which product is designed for this?
explanation: Shield Platform Encryption encrypts data at rest and has implications for features such as search, so it needs planning.

stem: Hiding a field from a page layout is enough to stop a user seeing the data anywhere. True or false?

options.text: False, field-level security is the real control
True, because a field that is not on the layout is hidden everywhere
True, but only in reports where layouts are applied
True, but only on mobile where layouts are applied

explanation: Page layouts only control the layout screen. The field can still appear in reports, list views and the API unless field-level security hides it.

objective: Respond to a suspected account compromise
stem: Which is the BEST first step when an admin suspects a user's account has been compromised?

options.text: Freeze the user and reset the password
Delete the user straight away so the account cannot be used
Wait and watch the login history for a week before acting
Change the org's currency so the user loses access to data

explanation: Freeze the account, reset the password, then check Login History and the audit trail before deciding next steps.

objective: Tell login IP ranges from trusted IP ranges
stem: Which TWO statements about login IP ranges are true? (Choose 2)

options.text: They are set on a profile
They block logins from outside the range
They apply to the whole org by default
They only prompt the user for a code

explanation: Login IP ranges belong to a profile and block logins from outside. Trusted IP ranges are org-wide and only skip verification.

stem: Which security layer controls which individual records a user can see?

options.text: Login IP ranges, which limit where users can log in
Password policy, which sets how often passwords change
MFA, which asks for a second proof of identity

explanation: The sharing model decides record visibility. Login controls decide who gets in at all.

stem: How long does standard Login History data stay available in Setup?

options.text: Seven days, after which it is removed from Setup
Forever, because Salesforce never removes login records
Five years, for audit and compliance reasons

explanation: Login History shows roughly the last six months. Download the data if you need to keep it longer.

stem: Which product keeps field history for years, beyond the standard retention?
explanation: Field Audit Trail is a paid add-on that extends field history retention.

stem: Users must be forced to log in only from the office network. Which is the most precise tool?

options.text: Login IP ranges on the profile

explanation: Login IP ranges restrict where a profile's users can log in from. Login hours restrict when.

stem: A user is locked out after repeated wrong passwords. Which admin action fixes it quickly?

options.text: Delete the user and create a new one
Change the OWD so that the user can log in
Clone the profile so that the user has a new one

explanation: Admins can unlock a locked-out user from the user record or the Users page.
